Sokolow Podlaski Old Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Sokołów Podlaski, Poland

Not demolished. Sokołów Podlaski's original Jewish cemetery (see the Sokołów Podlaski New Jewish Cemetery record for the town's fuller community history), presumably established at the end of the 16th or 17th century, remained active until the newer cemetery opened between 1880-1920. Postwar WWI funding from Bucze Rubinsztejn and the American Jewish Joint Distribution Committee added fencing, though the interwar period brought disrepair. During WWII, starost Ernest Gramss ordered tombstones removed for construction, including paving Węgrowska Street near the starosty office, with the work carried out by Jewish forced laborers; Germans also conducted executions on-site. Postwar, the grounds became a municipal park; a hotel and Sports and Recreation Centre pool were later built on the site. Several dozen recovered tombstones are stored at City Hall and the Museum of the Bug Lands in Sterdyń.
